newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh PM Hasina vows to end campus violence.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh PM Hasina vows to end campus violence.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, talking tough to those who tamper with law and order, vowed on Sunday to end violence on educational campuses, often the scenes of bloody clashes.

"Anyone to be found possessing illegal arms on educational campuses will be caught and punished, no matter which political party he belongs to," Hasina told a conference of her Awami League party's student front in Dhaka.
"A terrorist is a terrorist. He does not have any political or ideological identity," she said.
Police say at least 100 students die every year in armed clashes between rival student groups on the country's campuses.
Hasina, facing challenges both within and outside her party for her uncompromising stance on law and order, asked the police to take stern action against what she called terrorists.
"Discharge your duty with honesty and independently, without fear or favour. Earn people's trust and confidence," the prime minister told senior police officers on Sunday.

Hasina seemed undaunted by a dispute triggered by recent police actions in which the brother of a prominent legislator of the ruling Awami League was arrested for what police said were "acts of terrorism".
The legislator, Abdul Kader Siddiqui, has called the arrest of Azad Siddiqi a personal vandetta and demanded that Home (Interior) Minister Rafiqul Islam be sacked.

Awami sources said on Sunday Hasina was consulting fellow party leaders before taking any action against Kader Siddiqi, known as "Tiger Siddiqi" for his role as a guerrilla fighter in Bangladesh's 1971 independence war against Pakistan.
The opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) of former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia also complained of "mass arrest and persecution of BNP activists".
Hasina denied the allegation and said no one had been arrested on political grounds.
